segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Eleven. Construct a segment at right angles to a given line from a given point on it. Given segment A B and point C on it, we are to construct from C a segment perpendicular to A B.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Eleven. Construct a segment at right angles to a given line from a given point on it. Given segment A B and point C on it, we are to construct from C a segment perpendicular to A B.

segments.text: Take a point D at random on segment A C. By Proposition Three, cut off from C B a segment C E equal to C D. Next, by Proposition One, on segment D E construct the equilateral triangle F D E. Then, by Postulate One, construct the segment F C joining vertex F to point C.

subsegments.text: Take a point D at random on segment A C. By Proposition Three, cut off from C B a segment C E equal to C D.
Next, by Proposition One, on segment D E construct the equilateral triangle F D E.
Then, by Postulate One, construct the segment F C joining vertex F to point C.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Now compare triangles D C F and E C F: side D C equals E C, side C F is common, and base D F equals base F E. Therefore, by Proposition Eight, side-side-side congruence, the adjacent angles D C F and E C F are equal. By Definition Ten, when a segment standing on a line makes the adjacent angles equal, each angle is a right angle and the segment is perpendicular. Therefore segment C F has been constructed at right angles to segment A B from point C on it, as was required to do.
